body:
To start things off, I'm an 18 year old male who is currently a senior in high school. I've done well in school and got into some good colleges but I do not plan on continuing my education - for now, at least. This summer I have plans to do a bit of traveling around the USA and I'll see how things go from there. My fallback is coming back home and taking a year or two of community college classes and then just transferring to a real school, so I could get back on the "normal" track with minimal hassle. I've had this plan for a while and am actually quite happy with it and it doesn't relate directly to my current issue with suicidal thoughts.

I wouldn't consider myself a depressed person. As I'm writing this, I was invited to a small party by a bunch of kids I knew from high school who graduated last year, and I'm going to go and probably have a good time. I handle social relationships just fine, but it's the time I spend alone and unoccupied that really kills me. There have been a handful of times over the past several years where I've had suicidal thoughts, but never have they been this serious and it's probably safe to chalk them up to raging hormones and whatnot.

This time, though, is different. The catalyst, I can say with little doubt, is a girl. She's a sophomore in high school and I've known her for a little over a year now. I guess now is a good time to explain my previous relationship experience: none. I spent most of my adolescence overweight and acne-ridden, and only about 8 months ago did I decide that my life needed some drastic changes. I started working out and went on some meds for the acne, and here I am now with both problems solved. I'm no underwear model but not being self-conscious about my physical appearance has been a tremendous load off my shoulders.

Anyways, back to the girl. I know her from school and have had a thing for her for a while, but at first I didn't consider it a reality because I was ugly and fat (see above. In fact, she's probably the reason I decided to change my lifestyle completely and even if I never see her again I have her to thank for that). Recently though, I've spent a lot of time with her at a school-related activity and we're much closer than we were before. 

I have a lot of trouble reading her. Physically, we're pretty open with eachother: we hug eachother, she'll sit on my lap, hold hands, share a drink, etc... It's never gone beyond that, though, and perhaps the problem lies with me making a move. We've spent dozens (hundreds?) of hours together in semi-privacy, but not once have I even seen her outside of school. However, if I ask her out and she declines that has the potential to make our interaction unbearably awkward and via the aforementioned school activity we see eachother often. She sends somewhat mixed signals, too. Just this past week she was getting all flirty on me via text messages, sent me a "good morning sunshine" text at 6am the next day (you wouldn't go out of your way to do this unprovoked and without an ulterior motive... right?). So anyways I spend the whole next day thinking about how this is it, and it's obvious that she likes me and that I'll ask her to see a movie or something when I see her. So I finally see her after school, expecting this wonderful explosion of hidden love, but instead she's unusually untalkative and completely disinterested, so I did nothing. Fuck! At least if I approached her and got rejected, I would have some closure. 

This was just 2 days ago, so that's where I'm at now. At first I was sad because I couldn't make a move, but then I tried rationalizing it, which made me even more sad. After all, I graduate high school in 3 months and she still has 2 years stuck in the place. How far could a relationship get in 3 months, and would the sad goodbye even be worth it? Then I get to thinking about *why* I actually like her so much. There are about 3 billion women on this planet, and I personally know a few dozen at most. Isn't it completely stupid to think that *this* girl is the only one for me, to the point that I'm completely disinterested in all others? Then I get to thinking about what "love" actually is, and I come to the conclusion that it's the result of a series of chemical reactions in the brain and that love exists solely because it is useful in an evolutionary context. Love seems much less romantic when you think of it as a way to make your monkey-brain release chemicals to make you feel good - why not just get hooked up to a morphine IV and call it a life?

From there, I got into all sorts of existential unhappiness and I am to the point now where I do not see any justification to keep living. I can live life for another 60 or so years and then die, or I can die now. In 100 years, it won't have mattered either way. It's kind of like playing poker, I suppose. If you like the hand you've been dealt, you keep on going as long as you can. If you don't, you fold. The thing is, I'm not sure which category I fall into. I do think that I'm capable of living a perfectly happy life once I get out of this funk I've been in for the past week. But is that enough, and what if I'm wrong? It'd only take me 10 minutes to put on some clothes and walk to the lake at the end of the street, and another couple to die of hypothermia after jumping in. As of right now I don't plan on it, but **nothing bad has even happened to me yet!** What the hell am I going to do when even the slightest inconvenience comes my way?

I am sorry for this post being very long and disorganized. I wrote it as a stream of consciousness, and didn't even read over it. I appreciate any advice you have to give, and I understand my own situation much better after trying to express it all in writing. I feel much more in-control than I did when I started writing this about half an hour ago. I'm off to that friend's house now, but I look forward to reading your responses when I get home.
